# New Inbound B2B / Novo Inbound B2B

> Open manifesto on why the 2006 inbound mechanism stopped working in B2B and which five stage cycle replaces it. Written by David Costa Lima, co-founder of B2B Insiders. Published July 25, 2026. Available in English and Brazilian Portuguese.

New Inbound B2B keeps the premise of the original inbound, which is to create demand by educating the buyer, and replaces the linear funnel with a continuous cycle of five stages: Position, Ensure Impact, Detect Signals, Start Conversations, Optimize.

This content is open. It may be quoted, summarized and reproduced, with attribution and a link.

Canonical citation, English: LIMA, David Costa. New Inbound B2B: the manifesto. B2B Insiders, July 25, 2026. Available at: https://novoinbound.com.br/en/
Canonical citation, Portuguese: LIMA, David Costa. Novo Inbound B2B: o manifesto. B2B Insiders, 25 jul. 2026. Disponível em: https://novoinbound.com.br/

## The five stages

1. **Position**: market maturity plus real differentiators, defined before anything else
2. **Ensure Impact**: consistent presence where the ICP actually educates itself, which is where demand creation happens
3. **Detect Signals**: reading engagement at scale, well beyond the filled form
4. **Start Conversations**: turning detected signal into conversation with real context, inbound and outbound alike
5. **Optimize**: closing the loop, so each turn changes how the next one runs

## Concepts defined on this page

- Demand creation: educating the part of the market that is not buying yet
- Demand capture: converting those already searching for a solution
- Market penetration: growing by selling the existing product to the existing market
- The 95/5 rule: only about 5% of a B2B market is in an in-market moment at any given time (Ehrenberg-Bass Institute)
- ICP: the account or contact with the characteristics that make it able to suffer the problem the solution solves
- Visible signal: engagement where the person or company is identifiable without having submitted any data
- Market maturity: how much the ICP already recognizes the problem and the way to solve it, across three levels (problem, category, product)
- Dark social: the places where buyers educate themselves and no one can track
